items.q: Additional features in CTD are hypokalemia, hyperoxaluria and hyperuricosuria. Pick the ODD ONE OUT:
items.exp: CTD adds hypokalemia, hyperoxaluria, hyperuricosuria — not hyperkalemia. (Book p879)

items.q: The normal intact PTH range (pg/ml) is:
items.exp: iPTH normal range 50–100 pg/ml by 2nd gen immunoradiometric cold chain. (Book p879)

items.q: A ‘normal’ PTH value in the presence of raised serum calcium should make you suspect:
items.exp: High Ca2+ should inhibit PTH; a normal PTH with high Ca = suspect parathyroid-dependent causes. (Book p879)

items.q: iPTH >50 pg/ml profile — 1) Serum phosphate  2) 24 hr urine calcium … A) ↑↑  B) ↓
items.exp: Parathyroid dependent: S.phosphate ↓, 24 hr urine calcium ↑↑. (Book p879)

items.q: iPTH >50 pg/ml with ↓ phosphate and ↑↑ urine calcium points to:
items.exp: → Parathyroid adenoma, m/c inferior parathyroid gland. (Book p879)

items.q: Tc99 sestamibi scan (IOC for parathyroid adenoma) localizes the gland because it binds:
items.exp: Tc99 sestamibi binds with oxyphil cells; IOC for adenoma. (Book p879)

items.q: Vitamin D metabolites — 1) 25(OH)D3 ↑ + 1,25(OH)2D3 ↑  2) 25(OH)D3 N + 1,25(OH)2D3 ↑ … A) Tumor ↑1α-hydroxylase (lymphoma, acromegaly, sarcoidosis)  B) Hypervitaminosis D
items.exp: Both raised = hypervitaminosis D; 25 N with 1,25 ↑ = tumor ↑1α-hydroxylase. (Book p879)

items.q: Hypercalcemia with iPTH <20 pg/ml is related to:
items.exp: <20 pg/ml related to PTH-rp → paraneoplastic tumor, m/c SCC lung. (Book p879)
